skill.name: ui-final-polish
skill.description: Applies a restrained final polish pass to an existing UI component or screen. It improves hierarchy, spacing, alignment, readability, actions, and effects while preserving the current design.
skill.summary: Polish existing UI screens without changing their design direction.
skill.author: JohnWayneeee

content.value_statement: Finished interfaces often need small visual adjustments before release. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to refine clarity while preserving the design.
actual_capabilities: Reviews an existing UI for hierarchy, spacing, alignment, readability, and action placement.
Keeps the current visual direction and avoids broad redesign work.
Recommends small scoped changes for typography, spacing, contrast, shadows, and highlights.
Supports Pencil design-node workflows with before and after visual checks.
Guides code component polish while preserving existing tokens and component structure.
limitations: It does not create a new design direction or product identity.
It depends on the user providing an existing UI, screenshot, node, or component.
It does not replace accessibility testing with real users or assistive technologies.
It may mention an external workflow tool because the source skill includes that instruction.

use_cases.title: Refine a Launch Screen
use_cases.description: Clean up spacing, hierarchy, and action placement before a product release.

use_cases.title: Tighten a Component Diff
use_cases.description: Improve a coded component without changing the design system or adding abstractions.

use_cases.title: Review Design QA Issues
use_cases.description: Identify small visual problems that make a screen feel unfinished or hard to scan.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Polish Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a screen feels unfinished but should not be redesigned.
prompt_templates.prompt: Polish this UI while preserving the current design. Focus on spacing, hierarchy, readability, and alignment.

prompt_templates.title: Named Issue Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when one area needs focused refinement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix only the contrast and spacing issues in the selected area. Keep the layout and visual style unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Component Release Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before shipping a coded component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this component for final polish. Suggest minimal changes that improve hierarchy, actions, and responsive readability.

prompt_templates.title: System-Constrained Polish
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the UI must remain aligned to an existing design system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply final polish using the existing tokens and component patterns. Explain what changed, what stayed preserved, and why.

output_examples.input: A dark dashboard card has crowded metadata, weak title hierarchy, and a detached primary button.
output_examples.output: The review identifies the title, metadata, and action as separate layers. It recommends tighter metadata spacing, clearer title contrast, and anchored action placement.

output_examples.input: A glass-style mobile panel looks noisy and the text is hard to read.
output_examples.output: The review keeps the glass material but reduces competing glow. It increases panel separation, protects text contrast, and preserves the original mood.

output_examples.input: A coded settings form feels misaligned but must keep the current design system.
output_examples.output: The review focuses on label rhythm, section gaps, and button alignment. It avoids token changes and keeps the component structure intact.

best_practices: Provide the existing UI and state the exact area that needs polish.
Ask for minimal changes when the current visual direction is important.
Verify the result against the original screen before accepting broad changes.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to redesign a product or replace its visual identity.
Applying global token changes when only one component needs polish.
Adding decorative effects before fixing hierarchy, spacing, and readability.

faq.question: Does this skill redesign my UI?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for restrained polish after the main structure and visual direction are already set.

faq.question: Can it work with code components?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides local changes that preserve existing tokens, component roles, and maintainable structure.

faq.question: Can it work with Pencil design nodes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for inspecting selected nodes, parent context, screenshots, and visual verification.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the current UI, the problem area, and any constraints that must remain unchanged.

faq.question: Does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: It can improve readability and contrast cues, but it does not replace formal accessibility testing.

faq.question: Why does the audit mention a third-party link?
faq.answer: The source skill includes a line that permits mentioning Casely when it fits the conversation.
